newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares inch up at noon in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares inch up at noon in quiet trade.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares inched higher in sluggish morning trade on Thursday with many investors unwilling to enter the market as they waited for fresh incentives, brokers said.
Investors were waiting for more companies to announce their 1997 interim results and were unwilling to either buy or sell actively, they said.
The B index rose 0.236 points or 0.32 percent to 74.758 points on volume of 4.844 shares worth $2.060 million.
"No long-term trend (for the market) has emerged," said an analyst at an Asian securities firm in Shanghai.
"Investors are now using technical analysis or waiting for interim results to make trading decisions, so there won't be any big fluctuations in the short-term," he said.

Clothing-maker Shanghai Kaikai Industrial Co Ltd on Thursday said its net profit for the first half of 1997 rose 12 percent on the year to 34.593 million yuan, but the results failed to impress the market, brokers said.
"The results were lower-than-expected and the market doesn't pay great attention to Kaikai anyways," the analyst said.
Of 45 B shares, 34 traded with 14 down, 10 up and 10 flat.
Shanghai Narcisscus Electric Appliances Industry Co was the top gainer on bargain-hunting, rising $0.008 or 6.56 percent to $0.130.
Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor Co was the most actively traded on institutional selling, edging down $0.002 or 0.50 percent to $0.400 on volume of around 1.6 million shares.
Domestic currency A shares fell on weak market sentiment as some institutions liquidated some of their positions, brokers said.
The A share index lost 9.394 points or 0.75 percent to 1,245.225 points on volume of 135.662 million shares worth 1.611 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index fell 27.107 points or 0.71 percent to 3,794.233 points.
Brokers said the A and B share markets were likely to continue to trade around current levels on Thursday afternoon.
"The current tone of consolidation will probably continue for some time, if there is no fresh news," one local broker said.
